overviewHtml:
Managed environments multiply across production, staging and development, and answering one question means signing in to each in turn.

What you get

  • Terminal access to problems, entities, events, logs, metrics, SLOs and vulnerabilities
  • One named context per environment, with queries that fan out across all of them
  • Read-only contexts by default, running on your workstation
  • The same tool coverage as the Managed MCP server
getStartedHtml:
You need one or more Dynatrace Managed environments and an API token for each.

  1. Install dtmgd with Homebrew, a script or Go
  2. Create a context per environment and store its token
  3. Run the doctor check, then list open problems
